cards.note: The Amazonas 319 has a very lush, bright green and tropical landscape, as it cuts through the Amazon rainforest. The road is flat and mostly unpaved, featuring bright orange soil. However, closer to Manaus the road becomes paved. There are wooden or ladder poles alongside the entire stretch. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

This road is divided. What makes it special is that one direction as asphalt and the other direction has concrete pavement.

As of 2024, this does not apply to the entire road anymore, so you should not rule this road out if your loc doesn't have this meta.

The Pará section of the 163 is often hilly, curvy, dry, and sometimes hazy. It has a wide range of amazonian vegetation. The road is frequently trafficked, usually by transportation trucks. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

It’s also the Only road that has coverage in West Para
This road can be recognized by the Amazonian looking trees and the NW/SE angle. It always has Gen 4 and an exposed, blue car front.
This wide dirt road has Amazonian trees and a blurred car. You will not find other cars on the road. It's the only East-to-West angle road in that area.
This road looks like an Amazonian road with the trees and dense rainforest. It runs east-west, slightly to the south. The road looks like its stained with mud
This road is characterized by it's Amazonian look and the SW-NE road angle. Some sections of this road are overcast and/or showcase a flat landscape.

The 364 through Acre is very recognisable due to the rollercoaster-like landscape and road: the road uniquely rides the hills rather than snaking around them. There is usually no traffic, and is covered mostly by Generation 3 with an antenna.

This road in eastern Santa Catarina is characterized by its windyness and by the steep mountains and cliffs along its side. It can feel like your driving with the clouds. The road goes through Corvo Branco which is a famous tourist attraction.
This road east of Fortaleza is characterized by its unique pavement and the sanddunes along the road.

This part of the BR156 can be recognized by the Amapa Blur (slight blur at the front right of the blue-striped car). It's the only Amapa Blur coverage on a road that goes East-West. This part of the road is paved.
Flooded coverage can be found between Macau and Macauzinho in Rio Grande do Norte.
Most of this road has a thick (1m) stripe of red dirt on the sides of the road. The road is oriented North-South and frequently shows Babassu palms
This road is characterized by the Amapa Blur (slight blur at the front of a blue-striped car), the red, and the road angle to Northwest. There are frequently Areca palms growing near this road.
A very swampy road (PA-154) can be found Northwest of Belém. Notably, there are very few trees, and the soil is very red.
The road between Caico, RGDN and Santa Luzia, Paraiba is unique with its post bushfire coverage. The part in Paraiba often has outer dashed lines

This map west of the city of Rio de Janeiro is unique due to the water in the south, the roadlines (double yellow - double broken yellow - single broken white) and the little wall in the North. Rio mountains can be seen in most sections of the road to the north
Recognizable by the swamp-like landscape, the pine trees along the road and the Lagoon It runs at a SE-NW angle.

This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's more skinny and steeper.

This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's less skinny and less steep.
A road with a thin, red stripe out of gravel can be found east of Teresina, Piaui.
This road can be found North of Rio de Janeiro (city). It is a concrete road with black tar behind the road lines.
Smoke Coverage in Brazil can be found along the TO-335.
This beautiful road west of Cascavel and South of Toledo, by the PR-585 is characterized by the uneven red stone pavement and the sugarcane plantation next to it.
